examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Probability of a Normal Random Variable on a Bounded Interval
examples.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2),$ we have

$$
P(a <        X <        b) = P \left( \dfrac{a-\mu}{\sigma} <        Z <        \dfrac{b-\mu}{\sigma} \right)
$$

where $Z \sim N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu = 1$ and $\sigma = \sqrt 9 = 3.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.13<X<3.25) & =P(\frac{-1.13-1}{3}<Z<\frac{3.25-1}{3}) \\  & =P(-0.71<Z<0.75)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/a50513f550d8a3122e2f2276883a0189fe9bdc6dd19159e8ae94dbd5b247f5a9.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.71<Z<0.75) & =P(Z<0.75)-P(Z\le -0.71) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.75)-P(Z\le -0.71) \\  & =Φ(0.75)-Φ(-0.71)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.71) & =0.2389 \\ Φ(0.75) & =0.7734\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.71<Z<0.75) & =Φ(0.75)-Φ(-0.71) \\  & =0.7734-0.2389 \\  & =0.5345.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(-1.13<          X <          3.25) = 0.5345.
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $Y∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(Y\ge y)=P(Z\ge \frac{y-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =0$ and $\sigma =6.$

First, we transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge 12.18) & =P(Z\ge \frac{12.18-0}{6}) \\  & =P(Z\ge 2.03)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/c7af386057d2fba19697c0ad87c93a1865c69efaa1a5134f50bff6c7b9143dbe.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 2.03) & =1-P(Z<2.03) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 2.03) \\  & =1-Φ(2.03)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(2.03)=0.9788.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 2.03) & =1-Φ(2.03) \\  & =1-0.9788 \\  & =0.0212.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(Y\ge 12.18)=0.0212.
$$
